newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy suggests joint probe into Albanian shipwreck.
newsitem.headline: Italy suggests joint probe into Albanian shipwreck.

text.p: Italy, preparing to lead a multinational force into Albania, invited Tirana on Monday to join a probe into the sinking of a refugee ship and said relations between them must remain strong.
"The government wants to clear this up completely, absolutely, so that no shadow of a doubt remains," Prime Minister Romano Prodi told reporters.
"I am in favour of a bilateral Italo-Albanian effort to clarify thoroughly the facts."

Some politicians had expressed concern about the reception the force to protect aid deliveries would receive after some 83 Albanians were feared drowned in a collision between their boat and an Italian navy ship last week.
Four bodies were recovered on Friday and 34 people rescued. Italy has ruled out finding anyone else alive.

Far-right parliamentary deputy Alessandra Mussolini, grand-daughter of the late Italian dictator whose troops occupied the Balkan country in 1939, called for the mission to be delayed until the situation calmed.

"Now, more than ever, it is not possible to send our soldiers to Albania when we must first mend diplomatic relations between our countries," she said. "Unless we want to send so many young people to be massacred."
Prodi said however that the incident must not be allowed to taint previously close ties.

He asked Defence Minister Beniamino Andreatta to tell his Albanian counterpart that Italy was "ready to work together" on the investigation, adding: "There must not be any problems or dramas between our two countries."
The Defence Ministry said Andreatta had asked Albania to name a panel of experts and said all documents, including those under military secrecy, would be made available.

Admiral Guido Venturoni, the defence chief of staff, said the Albanian minister was expected in Rome on Tuesday to discuss both the sinking and the protection force. Other countries' representatives would arrive on Wednesday.
The government has insisted that the tragedy in the Adriatic, which Tirana says killed at least 83 people, makes the mission ever more urgent to stem a tide of refugees.
Prodi said at the weekend he hoped it could start as soon as possible but some said the task had become tougher.

"It will certainly make our mission in Albania more difficult because many Albanians will undoubtedly have negative feelings against us," centre-right opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi said in the southern port of Brindisi on Sunday.
The sunken Albanian harbour patrol vessel came from the southern rebel-controlled Albanian port of Vlore, one of the ports the force is supposed to secure.
About 7,000 people protested in Vlore on Sunday with some demonstrators making death threats against Italy.
Italian ships have been ordered by Rome to intercept Albanian boats heading for Italy and persuade them to turn back.
Berlusconi said the government must change its policies. "This blockade (must) be suspended absolutely because it is hard to see where it is leading us to," he said.
Prodi said the patrols were not organised to prevent Albanians entering Italy but to control their arrivals and combat organised crime cashing in on illegal immigration.

He said the naval actions had been agreed between Rome and Tirana. "We will have to reflect on the ways and means, and the investigation into the incident could be useful in clarifying how to proceed with the patrols," he added.
Junior Foreign Minister Piero Fassino said the boat tragedy must not be allowed to overshadow the huge efforts Italy had made to accommodate refugees in recent weeks.
"What happened in the Straits of Otranto cannot hide the fact that Italy has given shelter in a civilised fashion to almost 13,000 Albanians in just a few days," he said.
